editorial_thesis: Today’s strongest signals connect model routing, security monitoring, open runtimes, and embodied systems around one practical rule: make agent work observable, bounded, and resumable.

topic_groups.title: Agent Execution Economics
topic_groups.selection_rationale: A fresh model release turns worker/verifier routing into a measurable cost-and-latency experiment, extending yesterday’s model-choice coverage with a new fast execution tier.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen for Agentic Workflows
sources.why_selected: Fast model with 1M context, four thinking levels, and published execution economics.
sources.usefulness: Use Hydrogen for first-pass coding, extraction, and worker agents; reserve deeper models for planning and escalation.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen: Fast agentic development for coders
sources.why_selected: Shows parallel isolated workspaces and orchestration around the new model.
sources.usefulness: Map isolated workspaces to parallel client deliverables with a merge/review gate.

sources.title: State of Development 2026
sources.why_selected: Survey finds state tracking, debugging, and cost management are the main agent blockers.
sources.usefulness: Use the report as a checklist for Buildn adoption instrumentation, not as a benchmark.

topic_groups.title: Agent Security + Monitoring
topic_groups.selection_rationale: New independent-benchmark results make async anomaly detection concrete while exposing poisoned memory as a blind spot; this is a material update to prior security-control coverage.

sources.title: Agent Anomaly Detection on independent benchmarks
sources.why_selected: Private-preview detector flagged 87% of harmful instructions agents carried out; false alarms were 2–16%.
sources.usefulness: Add asynchronous trace review to Buildn runs and compare detections with deterministic outcome checks.

sources.title: SI Agent Standards Initiative
sources.why_selected: NIST prioritizes identity, authentication, agent-agent security, and interoperable protocols.
sources.usefulness: Use its pillars to structure client readiness reviews and Buildn’s authority model.

sources.title: Agentic AI Security 2026: OWASP Top 10
sources.why_selected: Goal hijack and tool misuse are useful threat categories for trace-based tests.
sources.usefulness: Translate categories into adversarial fixtures for agent workflows.

sources.title: Codex Security Cloud at DevDay
sources.why_selected: Cloud scanning, deduplication, and fix preparation show security work moving into unattended agent loops.
sources.usefulness: Compare scheduled security agents with human-reviewed remediation queues.

topic_groups.title: Open Agent Infrastructure
topic_groups.selection_rationale: NVIDIA’s new CNCF contributions materially change the open-infrastructure landscape: runtime governance, long-lived agent workloads, GPU scheduling, and fast recovery are being composed as shared layers.

sources.title: OpenShell contribution to CNCF
sources.why_selected: OpenShell enters CNCF Sandbox as a runtime for deterministic agent governance across cloud, on-prem, and hybrid environments.
sources.usefulness: Study it as a reference for policy-outside-the-agent and portable control planes.

sources.title: Agent Substrate + NVIDIA infrastructure
sources.why_selected: The stack targets suspend/resume, shared environments, inference serving, and cluster scheduling for long-lived agents.
sources.usefulness: Useful architecture reference for high-churn jobs and resumable sessions.

sources.title: NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine, Recipes, and Snapshot
sources.why_selected: Signed images, deployment recipes, and checkpointed inference restore target repeatable AI-factory operations.
sources.usefulness: Borrow the concepts of signed artifacts and fast recovery for client delivery.

sources.title: NIST agent identity and authorization concept
sources.why_selected: The standards effort connects runtime identity with delegated authority.
sources.usefulness: Use it to keep infrastructure portability from becoming credential sprawl.

topic_groups.title: Embodied Agents: Memory, Serving, Safety
topic_groups.selection_rationale: A neglected physical-systems lane earns inclusion because new work links three concerns that software agents also face: selective memory, cache-aware serving, and action-time safety gates.

sources.title: Serving Agentic Robot Fleets
sources.why_selected: At 32 robots, KV thrashing cut throughput from about 2.4 to 0.6 requests/s; admission control restored useful throughput.
sources.usefulness: Apply active-work caps and cache-aware scheduling to high-fanout agent jobs.

sources.title: Learning to Live: Lifelong Embodied Intelligence
sources.why_selected: LIFE combines event gates, source-preserving Plastic Memory, and reusable capability construction; its real-robot case reports 98.3% on six questions.
sources.usefulness: Use selective capture plus later evidence access for durable client/project context.

sources.title: LEASH: Stay Safe in Agentic Robotics
sources.why_selected: RoboRisk tests task refusal, plan repair, execution hazards, injection, and sequential memory; LEASH adds task, action, and commit gates.
sources.usefulness: Translate the three gates into plan approval, tool-call review, and irreversible-action confirmation.

sources.title: Embodied First Exam
sources.why_selected: A broad evaluation combines 26 adapted suites with nine new suites covering capability and safety.
sources.usefulness: Use as a reminder that agent quality needs multi-surface, not single-benchmark, evidence.
